title: Compact mode: sticky table headers, RTL scroll, and button density regressions on mobile Safari & Firefox
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: In compact density mode there are multiple cross-browser regressions affecting table headers, horizontal scrolling in RTL locales, and small-button hit targets on iOS Safari and Firefox for Android. This ticket consolidates reproduction steps, triage notes, proposed design fixes, and follow-up engineering tasks.

Affected components:
- Table (sticky header in compact mode, overflow behavior, header clipping)
- Buttons (compact size, hit area vs visual size)
- Tokens: density token interactions with spacing and header z-index
- Charts: minor clipping when embedded in compact table rows (observed on Safari mobile)

Observed behavior: 
1) Safari iOS 16/17: table header in compact mode uses position: sticky but gets clipped when parent has -webkit-overflow-scrolling or transform applied (header disappears on scroll or flick).
2) Firefox on Android: horizontal scrolling in RTL tables snaps incorrectly; scrollbars overlay controls and invisible padding allows touch events to miss table rows.
3) Compact buttons (visual 32px) have <44px touch targets on mobile due to negative margins used to achieve denser layout; causes frequent miss/tap failures and keyboard focus misses for screen reader users.
4) Charts embedded in compact table rows (sparkline cells) occasionally repaint and cause a 1px vertical shift on Safari when row heights change during scroll.

Steps to reproduce: 
- Device/Browser matrix: iPhone 12 (iOS 16), iPhone 14 (iOS 17 beta), Pixel 6 (Android 13) with Firefox Nightly.
- Open examples: https://redwood-internal/design-system/table#compact-density and open RTL locale sample.
- On mobile Safari: enable 3-4 rows with horizontal scroll, then perform quick flicks and observe header disappearance.
- On Firefox Android RTL: swipe horizontally and notice overscroll snap/jump and controls overlay.
- On any mobile: tab through compact buttons with VoiceOver/TalkBack and verify minimum 44px hit target.

Triage notes and immediate mitigations: 
- Root cause hypotheses: 
  * Safari sticky + transformed parent known issue (position: sticky fails when ancestor has transform or -webkit-overflow-scrolling).
  * Firefox RTL handling appears tied to scroll-snap/padding interaction and our custom scrollbar CSS.
  * Button hit target compromise introduced by compact density token that sets negative margins to collapse layout.
- Short-term mitigations (hotfix candidates): 
  * For Safari: force no-transform on immediate scroll container in compact table examples, or fall back to JS-based sticky shim for affected pages (ENG-59120 dependency).
  * For buttons: revert negative margin for mobile media query (max-width: 768px) to restore 44px tap area while keeping visual density via font-size/line-height tweaks.
  * For Firefox RTL: disable custom overlay scrollbar in RTL mobile builds as temporary patch and add a QA flag to test outcomes.

Design proposals (preferred): 
- Tables: maintain position: sticky but modify layout so the scrolling container is the element that has overflow (no transformed ancestor). Update table container token in compact mode to avoid transforms. Provide a JS fallback (sticky shim) gated by feature-detect and only enabled for iOS Safari when necessary.
- Buttons: update density token set to include 'touch-safe' variant automatically applied under 768px width that increases padding while keeping compact visuals via geometry + visual reduction (smaller border-radius, reduced icon size). Document and add examples in Figma and the component storybook.
- RTL scroll: remove absolute custom scrollbar overlays and rely on native scrollbars for mobile; adjust scroll-snap and padding math so that RTL content uses logical properties (margin-inline-start/end) and avoid pixel-snapping by rounding scroll offsets.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Repro steps no longer show header disappearance on iOS Safari for compact tables in our test matrix.
- Touch targets for compact buttons are >= 44px in mobile breakpoints and keyboard focus rectangles visually match.
- RTL horizontal scroll in Firefox Android behaves smoothly with no overlay on controls.
- No visual regressions introduced in desktop density modes.

Follow-ups for engineering & QA: 
- ENG to implement fallback & CSS token changes (ENG-59120, ENG-59205).
- QA to add automated cross-browser checks to Percy for compact table permutations and run Selenium/WebDriver tests for RTL scrolling.
- Design to update Figma tokens and provide migration notes for downstream consumers.

Links and references: 
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/redwood/design-system/compact-density
- Storybook examples: https://staging.redwood.dev/storybook/?path=/story/table-compact
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/Compact+Density+Behavior
- Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/3245 (button-density-revert-hotfix), https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/3251 (table-compact-sticky-shim)
comments: 2026-03-01 — Aisha Patel: Initial report captured during mobile QA pass; collected repro videos from 3 devices and attached links. Marked as P1 due to recurring customer reports from RTL locales.

2026-03-02 — Liam Chen: Confirmed sticky header disappears on iOS Safari when parent has transform: translateZ(0) used for GPU compositing. Created ENG-59120 for a CSS-first mitigation and flagged a JS fallback as backup.

2026-03-03 — Marisol Gomez (QA): Verified button tap misses on iPhone 12 when using compact buttons inside toolbars. Temporary workaround patch (PR #3245) restored tap area at mobile breakpoints; needs design approval for visual change.

2026-03-04 — Ethan Park (Engineering): Ran experiments removing custom scrollbar overlays in Firefox Android; observed improved RTL scroll behavior. Pushed prototype PR #3251 and requested design review for token changes.
2026-03-05 — Liam Chen: Updated acceptance criteria and added test matrix to Percy. Assigned final QA verification and scheduled a cross-team review on 2026-03-07.
2026-03-05 — Priya Nair (Accessibility): Reviewed proposed touch-safe variant — recommends adding explicit aria attributes for focus visibility and ensuring high-contrast outline in compact mode.
2026-03-05 — Aisha Patel: Uploaded repro media and added links to Confluence page. Marking this ticket In Progress; next: finalize density token changes and hand off to ENG-59120 and ENG-59205.
